sections.name: Looter
sections.card:
Summary: An enemy that runs away from you instead of fighting. Catch and kill it and it drops a Loot Crate plus 8 materials.
Tips: It can only appear from wave 3. Each time it gets a chance to appear, the odds are 10%: the first chance comes 25 seconds after a wave begins, and another every 15 seconds after that. The table gives it 5 health that grows by 30 each wave and a speed between 300 and 400, and lists your base speed as 450.

sections.name: Gobbler
sections.card:
Summary: An enemy that hunts down materials, eats them, and grows as it eats.
Weak points: Its first version is fast but fragile.
Tips: Killing it drops the materials it ate: all of them from its first version, twice as many from the second and three times as many from the third. The later versions are slower but have more health. It has only a 3% chance to appear, and the chance is rolled 10 seconds after a wave begins; it can turn up from wave 1.

sections.name: Slasher Egg and Slasher
sections.card:
Summary: A Slasher Egg sits still; leave it alone for 5 seconds and a Slasher hatches from it. A Slasher follows you but backs off when you get close, and hits with a vertical slash from medium range.
Weak points: An egg only hatches if it is still alive when its 5 seconds run out, so killing it first means no Slasher.
Tips: Neither is met on Danger 0: both start on Danger 1, Slashers from wave 4 and eggs from wave 7. A Slasher starts with 50 health and gains 25 each wave, while an egg starts with 5 and gains 3.

sections.name: Pursuer
sections.card:
Summary: A chaser that hurts you on touch and gets faster with every second it keeps chasing you.
Tips: It first appears at wave 11, where the page works its health out as 250 (10 to start plus 24 for each wave after the first), and that is 40% higher on Danger 5. Its speed climbs from 150 to 600 while the page gives your own base speed as 450, and its speed does not change with the wave or the Danger level.

sections.name: Fly
sections.card:
Summary: An enemy that moves around you. When your ranged weapons hit it, it answers half the time by shooting out projectiles in random directions.
Tips: The 50% chance applies to ranged hits only, because hits from melee weapons do not make it fire. It starts with 15 health and gains 4 each wave, moves at a random speed between 325 and 375, and is only met from Danger 1 up, starting at wave 4.

sections.name: Monk
sections.card:
Summary: An Elite enemy (Danger 2 and up) that opens by putting 15 Slasher Eggs on the field, then shoots at you, and later runs away while spawning Tentacles.
Tips: Its eggs hatch into Slashers after 5 seconds unless they are killed first. From 10 seconds in it fires 5 shots a second at you, and from the 30-second mark it spends 10 seconds running away and spawning Tentacles before going back to shooting. A Tentacle follows you, backs off if you get close, and attacks in a V shape at medium range. Killing the Monk drops a Legendary Loot Crate holding a guaranteed Legendary (tier 4) item.

sections.name: Gargoyle
sections.card:
Summary: An Elite enemy (Danger 2 and up) that attacks by throwing out circles and bursts of projectiles, in three stages.
Tips: At first it wanders at random, putting out a big circle of projectiles around itself every 0.3 seconds. From 60% health or 30 seconds in, it chases you and fires 12 projectiles around itself at random, every 0.4 seconds. From 30% health or 45 seconds in, it chases you and shoots projectiles off in random directions, once every 0.01 to 0.15 seconds. Killing it drops a Legendary Loot Crate holding a guaranteed Legendary (tier 4) item.

sections.name: Bait
sections.card:
Summary: A cheap Tier 2 damage item with a catch: it sends Lampreys after you at the beginning of the next wave.
Uses: It gives +8% damage and costs 25. Killing the Lampreys it brings pays 7 to 8 extra materials.
Tips: Between 7 and 8 Lampreys come at you, and the page calls them quite dangerous. A Lamprey charges at you every 1.5 seconds and fires projectiles out to either side as it goes.

sections.name: Metal Detector
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that gives the materials you pick up a chance to count double.
Uses: Each one adds 5% to the chance that a picked-up material is worth double, both as money and as experience. It also gives +6 Luck and +2 Engineering and takes away 5% damage. It costs 40, and you can hold up to 20.
Tips: Bagged materials paid out at the start of a wave are worth 4 times as much when it triggers, so you end up with about the same on average whether you let them get bagged or not. The same 4 times applies to Buccaneer's double materials. The page calls it very powerful for Endless Mode.

sections.name: Recycling Machine
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that raises how much you get back when you recycle weapons and items.
Uses: Without it, recycling returns 25% of an item's price. The machine adds 35%, so you get 60% back. It costs 35, and you can only hold one.
Tips: Entrepreneur's +25% stacks with it for 85% back. The payout follows an item's current price, so it grows with inflation and shrinks if you hold Coupons.

sections.name: Piggy Bank
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that adds 20% to the materials you carry out of the shop at the start of every wave.
Uses: Leave the shop holding 100 materials and the wave starts with 120. The bonus is money only, with no experience. It costs 40 and you can hold one. In Endless Mode it stops working after wave 20.
Tips: The gain compounds: any materials you hold back more than double within four waves and grow about 6.2 times over ten. It is best bought early and saved up, and the page suggests skipping it if you cannot save between rounds. It suits Demon and Streamer, and Saver begins with it.

sections.name: Scared Sausage
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 1 item that gives your hits a chance to set enemies on fire.
Uses: Each one gives hits a 25% chance to burn, so holding 4 reaches 100%. The burn deals 1 + (100%) damage every second, lasting at most 3 seconds, as the page writes it. It costs 25 and the limit is 4.
Tips: It also adds 1 to the damage of any other burn, such as the Flamethrower or Incendiary Turret, but a point of Elemental Damage is cheaper than the item, so it is not worth buying just for that. Engineering structures can burn enemies, and so can explosions from Bull, Landmines and Rocket Launcher. Baby Elephant, Cyberball and Riposte cannot, and neither can explosions from Spicy Sauce or Rip and Tear.

sections.name: Silver Bullet
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 3 damage item that multiplies your damage versus Elites and bosses.
Uses: Each one raises your damage versus Elites and bosses by 25%, applied on top of your other damage bonuses. It costs 70.
Tips: In the page's example, an attack that does 100 damage and reaches 200 with 100% Damage gets to 250 with one Silver Bullet, and to 400 with four. Jack's +125% bonus versus bosses and Elites is the same effect and adds to it.

sections.name: Coupon
sections.card:
Summary: A cheap Tier 1 economy item that makes the items in the shop cost less.
Uses: Each Coupon takes 5% off shop item prices, and you can hold up to 5 for 25% off. It costs 15.
Tips: No other item changes shop prices, and this one does not change what rerolls cost. With the character Entrepreneur and 5 Coupons the cut reaches 50%, the most possible. The page ranks it with the stronger items and says it is nearly always worth buying, unless it is first seen around waves 16 to 18 or after.

sections.name: Medikit
sections.card:
Summary: A Tier 4 healing item that gives a large amount of health regeneration, and more of it as each wave goes on.
Uses: It gives +10 HP Regeneration, plus another +2 for every 5 seconds that pass in a wave until that wave ends, and takes away 10 Luck. It costs 95 and is unlocked by winning a run with Doctor.
Tips: The page's table shows the extra regeneration reaching +34 by the 85-second mark, which it calls very potent for the wave 20 boss fight, a fight that lasts 90 seconds.
